subject.title: feat(cli): `skills uninstall` design proposal + prior art reconciliation

question: Should OpenClaw add a destructive `openclaw skills uninstall` CLI now, and what exact semantics should it use for manual/non-ClawHub skills, owner-qualified refs, `--global`/`--agent`, confirmation, dry-run, and JSON output?
rationale: The source-backed gap is real, but the command deletes workspace files and mutates lockfile state, so automation should not pick a permanent user-facing contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor Narrow CLI Uninstall
options.body: Land a focused CLI/lifecycle implementation that removes only provenance-verified ClawHub installs, cleans lockfile entries, documents behavior, and covers safety cases with tests.

options.title: Gateway Or Lifecycle First
options.body: Hold the CLI command until maintainers settle a shared Gateway or lifecycle API so dashboard/operator surfaces and CLI semantics align.

options.title: Defer The Command
options.body: Keep manual removal documented for now and close or pause implementation until stronger user demand justifies a destructive core command.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Narrow CLI Uninstall
recommendation.body: Land a focused CLI/lifecycle implementation that removes only provenance-verified ClawHub installs, cleans lockfile entries, documents behavior, and covers safety cases with tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced the skills CLI/native ClawHub install surface and is the strongest available history signal for deciding whether this belongs in core CLI now.
